### [Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04473>)

Megatron-LM combines tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, using interleaved pipeline stages and communication optimizations to distribute very large models across GPU clusters. It provides a foundational framework for choosing a parallelism configuration by balancing model memory, communication, and time spent waiting between pipeline stages.

**Published:** 2021-04-09 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Distributed Training, Tensor Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04473>) · [Code](<https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The SC 2021 paper analyzes parallelism and microbatch tradeoffs, then benchmarks training iterations for models up to one trillion parameters on as many as 3,072 A100 GPUs; component experiments examine communication and pipeline scheduling.

**Limitations:** These are historical systems measurements, not current hardware rankings or proof that a trillion-parameter model was trained to convergence. The best configuration depends on cluster topology, model shape, and batch size.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [DCP: Addressing Input Dynamism In Long-Context Training via Dynamic Context Parallelism](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10620>)

Dynamic Context Parallelism partitions attention into small blocks and replans their placement for each batch's sequence lengths and attention masks. It reduces unnecessary cross-GPU communication and balances variable-length workloads, making long-context training more efficient when static parallelism wastes resources.

**Published:** 2025-10-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Context Parallelism, Long Context, Distributed Training

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10620>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper provides a hypergraph-based planner, execution design, attention microbenchmarks, and end-to-end 8B-model experiments on 64 A100 GPUs; reported training speedups reach 1.16x for causal masks and 1.46x for sparse masks.

**Limitations:** The causal-mask range includes 0.94x slowdowns; benefits depend on sequence variability, mask sparsity, planning resources, and communication overlap. Public implementation was not verified.
